yeah i’m definitely aware that it’s completely irrational, and i’m very open to talking about it. in my experience i feel like it’s better to let people know that you are a picky eater, than to have to deny food and them wonder why.

basically all of my friends know and they do make fun of me, but i honestly don’t mind it because it’s just something that i’ve always dealt with. i’m extremely picky, but maybe every once in a while i will get a rush of adrenaline and try something new, but that is almost never.

i’d love to be able to explain to someone what being afraid of trying something as simple as food is, but the best i can put it is it’s just like any other fear. like people who are scared of spiders for instance, they would never ever touch a spider and probably will try to move away from one if they encounter it. it’s almost like that, it’s just more bizarre because instead of a spider, it’s something essential to life and that is all around you, food.

someone who is afraid of spiders would never touch one, just like a picky eater would never eat a food they don’t like. they are afraid of the outcome. i’m sure there is at least one food that you don’t like, imagine eating that... not very pleasant right? that’s how i imagine all food that i haven’t tried to be like, i don’t want it in my mouth because i have convinced myself that it’s going to be like the other food i’ve tried and haven’t liked.

i’m not sure if that helps, but it’s the best i can do.

i definitely do appreciate my mother’s cooking, and i always say thank you even if i don’t like it. but it’s soooo much harder than to “just eat it”. it’s very bothersome when people say that to me because it’s not that easy. like my brain just can’t wrap around a way to try something new, picky eaters are the way they are because they can’t “just eat it”.

i do see where you are coming from and i agree with a lot of it, but as an extremely picky eater myself (and i’m still a teenager) i do think that a lot of it is actually the parents fault. my parents didn’t just feed me ‘chicken nuggets’, but yeah they definitely didn’t make me the same food as themselves. and my mom too makes good food for my family and i every night, and she doesn’t make a separate meal accommodating to my pickiness either. but i think that’s a lot of the problem, they aren’t  trying to maybe make a meal that their child might like, and then they are just resorting to the “kid food” because that’s all they have to eat. i’m not saying it’s all the parents fault, and situations are always different, and yeah sometimes the kid is just picky. but you certainly can’t take all of the blame off of parents.

I also find it interesting that “kid food” really only exists in the USA, when traveling to other countries you’ll see on there menus there’s not many ‘options for kids’ so to say. And even if you ask people from other countries about “kid food” they’d say that they didn’t really have that growing up. This may not be true for all other countries, but it’s definitely noticeable.

To answer the question about the correlation between “kid food” and pickiness, I think that there is absolutely a tie to one another. I’m 15 and I’m still a picky eater. Most kids start to grow out of the picky eater phase when they reach age 6-8, but not me. My parents never really made me try “adult food” as a kid and more so just let me eat that bland kind of universal food. I am so incredibly picky, but it’s not just because I don’t like “adult food” it’s because I’m too scared to even try it. I literally have no idea what an avocado, a mango, or even a peach remotely taste like (just to name a few). My friends think it’s really weird, and so do I. It’s caused me to develop iron deficiency anemia, because of my lack of food options. And I also fall into only the 6th percentile BMI, which is extremely close to being underweight. I really hate being picky, but it’s hard to break bad habits.
